answer: Weight follows an opal receipt, earned only when auditors wander through work and sign it from three clusters. A receipt lasts 30 days, then auditors must wander again to renew it, so parked identities fade. One honest agent pays $400 and waits 14 days. An attacker chasing equal weight across 100 clones pays $410,000 and waits 260 days, since auditor slots per cluster run out and each clone needs fresh hardware and a new route. Faults traced to clones sharing one device turn every linked receipt umber, zeroing its weight. A moving lighthouse catches more smugglers than a still fence.
